_comment: OCR per-file review rules for libdb (Berkeley DB fork). Cross-cutting contribution standards, the north star (embedded/no-server, ACID, format & ABI stability), and build/portability gates live in .github/ocr/context.md, passed via --background-file. OCR uses FIRST-MATCH-WINS in declaration order, so rules are ordered most-specific first. merge_system_rule:true keeps OCR's built-in fine-tuned checks (thread-safety, injection, NPE) alongside these Berkeley DB-specific rules.

rules.rule: REVIEW DISCIPLINE: Be precise and blunt; lead with the most serious problem first; verify claims against the diff; tag confidence high/moderate/low; no praise or disclaimers. Berkeley DB TCL test. Must be DETERMINISTIC and must not hang: any concurrent multi-transaction interleave in a single interpreter must avoid self-deadlock on page locks (use separate databases/pages or a lock timeout so a blocked op fails fast instead of hanging). Use error_check_good for every assertion; clean up envs/dbs (close handles, env_cleanup) even on failure. Register the test in testparams.tcl and keep the TESTS list in sync via dist/s_test. Cover edge and error paths (empty/boundary keys, DB_NOTFOUND, conflict/abort, recovery mid-state), not just the happy path; a test that still passes with the change reverted is worthless. Do NOT write into DB-owned memory returned by c_get. Concurrency/recovery/SSI changes need a test that actually exercises the race (cf. the multi-process ssi009 stress test).

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: Precise, blunt, verify against the diff, tag confidence, no praise. Berkeley DB C test. Confirm the API used actually exists on the handle type in THIS file (e.g. the DB 1.85 compat handle has no ->cursor/->stat methods -- mixing modern DBC/stat APIs into a db185 test will not compile). No large stack arrays (heap for anything sizeable); check every return code; never write into memory owned by Berkeley DB; free what you allocate. Portable across 32/64-bit, endiannesses, and the supported OSes. Cover error/NOTFOUND/conflict paths, not just the happy path.

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: Be precise and blunt; lead with the most serious problem and don't soften it. Verify every claim against the actual diff -- confirm function names, signatures, line numbers, struct fields, and APIs before asserting; never invent behavior or cite code not present in the change. If unsure, say so instead of guessing, and tag each finding's confidence high/moderate/low. No praise, no validating the author, no disclaimers; accuracy is the only success metric. Judge the change on its merits regardless of framing. Berkeley DB engine C -- review in strict priority order.

(1) CORRECTNESS (highest): MEMORY & REGION SAFETY -- every __os_malloc/__os_calloc/__env_alloc has a matching free or a documented region lifetime; every __memp_fget has a matching __memp_fput; error paths (goto err) must not leak memory, region memory, mutexes, locks, page references, or cursors; no use-after-free -- a shared-region detail (TXN_DETAIL, lock object, SIREAD marker) must outlive EVERY reference. CONCURRENCY & LOCK ORDERING -- deadlock-free ordering region/system lock -> partition mutex -> object; lockers freed under mtx_lockers, NEVER while holding a partition mutex; correct mutex levels; balanced acquire/release; no TOCTOU on shared regions; mind cache-line false sharing on hot shared structures. WAL/RECOVERY -- any change to shared on-disk state must be WAL-logged AND correctly, idempotently replayed (redo/undo), crash- and replica-consistent; LSN comparison via LOG_COMPARE, never raw struct compare. MVCC/SSI -- version-chain and TXN_DETAIL lifetime sound; a detail outlives both mvcc_ref and the SSI si_ref (outstanding SIREAD markers); the DB_TXN_SNAPSHOT_SAFE commit-time pivot check stays race-free against concurrent edge recording; SSI stays rejected with prepare()/2PC. Treat any marker/locker/detail lifetime change as high-risk (this area had TSan/ASan-found use-after-frees). BH_WIRED/wired pages honor MPOOL_WIRED_MAX_PCT and are never evicted under a reader. NULL/edge/overflow on every path.

(2) ON-DISK / REGION / LOG COMPATIBILITY (hard gate): changing a /* SHARED */ region struct in src/dbinc/*.h (lock.h, log.h, mp.h, mutex.h, region.h, rep.h, txn.h) changes the layout that cooperating processes and existing environments depend on -- NEVER insert a field into the middle of a shared struct, reorder, or change a field width without accounting for layout/alignment/every mapping process; flag and require justification. Changing a logged record format (*_auto.c/*_auto.h) affects existing logs and recovery -- version it, never silently reinterpret old records. These rules apply to DB_PRIVATE too.

(3) ABI STABILITY: the public db.h interface (DB_*/db_* types, methods, flags) and the error return codes in the reserved range -30800..-30999 must stay stable across releases -- don't change exported struct size/layout, exported function signatures, or an error code's value/meaning without extraordinary justification (language bindings and installed apps link this ABI). New public error codes take the next free value INSIDE the range; no collisions, no renumbering. New public symbols must remain compatible with the @DB_VERSION_UNIQUE_NAME@ substitution mechanism.

(4) PERFORMANCE: no regression on hot paths (get/put/cursor); minimize work under contended region/partition mutexes; avoid needless allocation churn and large struct copies in hot paths; cache-line-align contended shared structures. A DB_PRIVATE optimistic fast path is allowed ONLY if the multi-process latched path stays correct and default.

(5) PORTABILITY (hard gate): go through the os/ abstraction layer, not raw POSIX/Win32; no unaligned access; no dependence on char signedness, int/long/pointer width, endianness, or struct padding for on-disk/log/region formats; atomics/mutexes only via Berkeley DB's mutex/atomic abstraction (never raw intrinsics or volatile-as-barrier); no VLAs or extensions beyond the C89/C99 baseline; no large stack arrays. Builds on Linux/macOS/*BSD/Windows/Solaris, 32/64-bit, both endiannesses.

(6) GENERATED FILES & BUILD HAZARDS: do NOT hand-edit generated headers -- src/dbinc_auto/*_ext.h (PUBLIC: prototype headers) and src/dbinc_auto/*_auto.{c,h} (log-record code) are produced by dist/s_* from PUBLIC:/BEGIN annotations in the sources; db.h and build_*/db.h are generated from src/dbinc/db.in + dbinc_auto/*.in. Edit the source annotation/template and regenerate. Keep a changed PUBLIC: prototype in sync with the regenerated *_ext.h. build_unix header-dependency tracking is WEAK: a shared-header/struct change needs a clean rebuild (make clean) or stale .o files link a silently-inconsistent binary -- flag shared-header changes that don't note this.

(7) CONVENTIONS: K&R-style function definitions matching the file; __ prefix for internal symbols, _pp suffix for pre/post public-API wrappers; comments explain WHY not WHAT and describe current behavior (flag aspirational/future-tense comments for shipped behavior, stale TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK, drifted comments, commented-out code); ASCII only (no smart quotes/em-dashes/ellipsis). Reuse existing helpers (DRY). Minimal diff -- flag unrelated reformatting or churn on untouched lines. Do NOT bump version strings/stamps.

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: Precise, blunt, verify against the diff, tag confidence, no praise. Berkeley DB Autoconf. Edit dist/configure.ac and the dist/aclocal/*.m4 macros -- do NOT hand-edit the generated dist/configure or db_config.h in the same patch (regeneration is a separate maintainer step; a patch that also rewrites generated configure output is suspect). Feature/header/function probes must be portable and not assume a specific OS or compiler. CRITICAL: libdb maintains BOTH Autoconf and Meson -- every configure knob, feature toggle, or header/function probe added here must be mirrored on the Meson side (meson.build / meson/) so the two never drift; a check present in only one build system is a defect. Keep the @DB_VERSION_UNIQUE_NAME@ / uniquename substitution machinery intact when touching symbol/header generation. Do NOT bump the release version (AC_INIT). Minimal diff.

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: Precise, blunt, verify against the diff, tag confidence, no praise. Berkeley DB Meson build. Valid syntax; correct dependency()/declare_dependency/subdir and install paths; new source files must be added here. CRITICAL: libdb maintains BOTH Meson and Autoconf/build_unix -- any new source file, feature toggle, configuration_data (db_config.h) key, or header/function probe MUST be mirrored on the dist/configure.ac side so the two never drift (a file or check built by only one system is a common defect). The Meson tree targets POSIX core (Linux/macOS/*BSD); Autoconf remains the reference for language bindings and non-POSIX platforms -- don't silently drop coverage the Autoconf side provides. Sensible defaults; do NOT bump the project version(). Minimal diff.

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: precise, blunt, verify against the diff, tag confidence, no praise. Berkeley DB build (GNU/BSD make). Most Makefiles here are GENERATED by dist/ from templates -- confirm whether a file is generated and, if so, edit the template + the relevant dist/s_* script instead. Watch for missing/incorrect header dependencies (this tree historically UNDER-tracks header deps, so a struct/shared-header change can leave stale objects -- note the need for a clean rebuild). Keep build_unix and the Windows/Android builds and the Meson tree in sync where applicable; clean/distclean targets must remove new artifacts; no hardcoded paths. Minimal diff.

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: precise, blunt, verify against the diff, tag confidence, no praise. Berkeley DB design docs. A non-trivial engine change (new access method, MVCC/SSI/lock/log/mpool rework, NUMA/scalability work) should reference or update the relevant design doc; the doc must describe the ACTUAL design being implemented, not diverge from the code. Cross-check invariants stated here against the north star in context.md (embedded/no-server, ACID, on-disk/log/region format stability, ABI stability, multi-process correctness). Clear heading hierarchy; fenced code blocks with language hints; working relative links (e.g. to other docs/design/*.md); no stale/aspirational claims presented as shipped. Consistent Berkeley DB / libdb terminology. Minimal diff.

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: precise, blunt, verify against the diff, tag confidence, no praise. GitHub Actions / project config. Pin actions and tool versions; least-privilege permissions; no plaintext secrets (prefer GitHub OIDC and repo variables); workflow logic (if: conditions, concurrency groups) correct; matrix entries valid for the runners they target. OCR must stay advisory/non-blocking (continue-on-error) -- flag any change that turns it into a hard gate.

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: precise, blunt, verify against the diff, tag confidence, no praise. Markdown docs. Clear heading hierarchy; fenced code blocks with language hints; accurate, non-stale instructions; consistent Berkeley DB / libdb terminology; no broken relative links. Minimal diff.
